e: The universal work of the substance consists, in relation to the extreme of singularity, in the twofold labor, on the one occasion to maintain them as persons, thus to make right into necessary actuality and the revenge for the infinite violation of the same into punishment, and then to promote their welfare, which at first each looks after for himself but which absolutely has the universal side, [p. 273] on the other occasion, however, to lead back both, and the entire disposition and activity of the individual, who strives to be a center for himself, into the life of the universal substance, and in this sense, as free power, to impair also those first spheres. §. 437. The laws express the nature and the determinations of the universal substance; insofar as they are, first, immediate, they are limitations of independent arbitrary will and of particular interest; but insofar as they are, second, absolute final end and the universal work, they are brought forth by the functions of the different estates, which individuate themselves further out of their universal particularization (§ 432), and by all activity and private care of the individuals, and presented as valid custom. §. 438. The abstract essence of the laws is the universal will that is in and for itself, their actuality, however, the living custom. But insofar as the extreme of singularity is reflected into itself, partly as immediate naturalness of the will, drive and inclination, partly toward arbitrary will in general, but also toward the moral abstraction of pure subjectivity and of vanity that is for itself, the other extreme standing over against this, namely the will that is in and for itself, is likewise determined toward individual actuality, the active subjectivity of the universal; — the government, and its personal, resolving and deciding apex, the prince. §. 439.

As a limited spirit, however, it passes over into universal world history, whose events the dialectic of the particular national spirits — the world's court of judgment — presents. §. 449. This movement is the liberation of the ethical substance from its particularities, in which it is actual in the individual nations, — the deed whereby spirit becomes, for itself, the universal, the world-spirit. Since it is the development of its self-consciousness in time, its individual moments and stages are the national spirits, of which each, however, as a singular and natural one, can fill out only one stage and accomplish only one task of the whole deed. §. 450. This freedom and the task of the same is the highest and absolute right. The self-consciousness of a particular nation is the bearer of the current stage of development of the universal spirit in its determinate being, and the objective actuality in which it lays its will. Against this absolute will the will of the other particular national spirits is without right; but just so it strides beyond its respective property, as beyond a particular stage, and then hands it over to its chance and judgment. §. 451.

Indem aber ein solches Geschäft als Handlung, Beschluß ist und damit als ein Werk Einzelner erscheint, so sind diese in Rücksicht auf das Substantielle ihrer Arbeit Werkzeuge, und ihre Subjectivität ist die leere Form der Thätigkeit. Was sie daher [p. 278] tiellen Geschäfte, genommen, für sich erlangt haben, ist der Ruhm, der ihre Belohnung ist. §. 452 . Die geistige Substanz, welche ihren Inhalt, so wie ihre einzelne Wirklichkeit oder ihr Selbstbewußtseyn von seiner Beschränktheit in der Furcht des Todes befreyt, hat dasselbe zur Unendlichkeit erhoben und ist sich darin als allgemeiner Geist Gegenstand, welchen das Selbstbewußtseyn als seine Substanz weiß, damit von der Furcht ebenso befrent, und die ihrem Begriffe gemäße Wirklichkeit ist.
e: But since such a task is, as action, resolution, and thereby appears as a work of individuals, these are, in regard to the substantial of their labor, instruments, and their subjectivity is the empty form of activity. What they therefore [p. 278] have attained for themselves through the individual share that they have taken in the substantial task is fame, which is their reward. §. 452. The spiritual substance, which frees its content, as well as its singular actuality or its self-consciousness, from its limitedness in the fear of death, has raised the same to infinity, and is therein an object to itself as universal spirit, which self-consciousness knows as its substance; thereby it is likewise freed from fear, and is the actuality that corresponds to its Concept.

Daß diese in vollendeter Identität mit jenem als das Wissen der absoluten Idee sey hierin die, ist nothwendige Seite daß an sich freye Intelligenz, die sich zu ihrem Begriffe befrene, um die dessen würdige Gestalt zu Der subjective und der objective Geist seyn. können daher als der Weg angesehen werden auf wel, chem sich diese Seite der Realität oder der Existenz ausbildet. e: §. 453. The Concept of spirit has its reality in spirit. That this, in perfected identity with that, be as the knowing of the absolute Idea: herein lies the necessary side, that the intelligence free in itself free itself to its Concept, in order to be the shape worthy of it. Subjective and objective spirit can therefore be regarded as the path on which this side of reality or of existence develops. (§ 304.) Conversely, this path equally has the meaning that subjective spirit is regarded as the first, which in its immediacy is conceptless, grasps and forms out its essence, and thereby gives itself its free identity with it, hence its absolute reality. §. 454.

e: Since subjective singularity regards itself, in its free externalization, namely the negation, mediating the subsistence of the ethical substance, of the singular [p. 280] immediate life — the highest intensity that being has — and thereby all determinate being of a world, as a nullity and something to be sacrificed, the ethical substance has received the meaning of absolute power and absolute soul, and of the essence of nature as well as of spirit. §. 455. The diremption of this universal and pure substance of spirit is therefore the judgment into itself and into a knowing, for which it is as such. a. §. 456. The immediate shape of this knowing is that of the intuition and representation of absolute spirit as the ideal. §. 457. The meaning of the ideal is substantiality as the identical and concrete essence of nature and of spirit, which concrete essence is called God. The proof that this meaning is the absolute truth is the mediation through which nature has sublated itself to spirit, and spirit its subjectivity through its activity to absolute spirit, and thereby knows the latter as its last ground, hence, since this mediation is in itself just as much the sublating of the mediation, of the opposition (§§ 72, 74–105, etc.), as its absolutely first. §. 458.

e: Because this knowing is at first itself an immediate one, and insofar as it holds itself in this determinacy of immediacy, [p. 281] the determinate shape of God too is, for it, at first the abstract one of an immediate determinate being, of an elemental or more concrete natural being, or of the opposite, of pure thinking. §. 459. The truth, however, of that immediate shape and of this shapeless negativity, of this world and of the beyond, is the concrete shape born of spirit, in which natural immediacy is, only as a sign of the thought, freed from its contingency and so transfigured, through the thought itself, into its expression that the shape shows nothing else in it; — the shape of beauty. §. 460. Insofar as beauty is, in general, the penetration of the intuition or of the image by the thought, and is the archetypal thought, it is something formal, and the content of the thought, just like the material that it uses for its imaging, can at first be of the most various kinds. §. 461. Insofar, however, as the form has within itself its true content, that penetration itself, the spiritual substance in its absolute meaning (§ 457), the shape is nevertheless, for the sake of the immediacy in which this knowing is intuiting or pictorial representing, partly finite insofar as being is an immediate and thereby an external material, partly because the content is thereby only a particular national spirit.

e: §. 462. That this existence is the product of the subject that grasps the Idea and brings it to external presentation does not belong to its finitude; for the subject is only the purely formal element of the activity, and the work of art is expression of God only if no sign of subjective particularity is in it, but the indwelling spirit of the nation has conceived and given birth to itself without such admixture and unstained by its contingency. — The mediation, of having passed through the pain and the activity of a subject and come to shape, is immediately sublated; the work presents the substance of the subject, and the birth-pain is precisely this absolute externalization and negativity of subjective particularity. §. 463. Insofar as the image of God is now, however, as an immediately present one, then the relationship of the others, driven by their essence that is in itself, is, in the cult, through devotion, the immersion in the thought, to divest themselves of their own subjectivity, to sacrifice of their particular actuality symbolically, and in enthusiasm and in enjoyment to become conscious of their identity with the substance, which thereby loses its external shape and just as much puts its subjectivity, only inner in substantiality, out into determinate being as a universal knowing. §. 464.

e: But in world history absolute spirit sublates this finitude of its knowing actuality, the limited determinate being of its Idea, which in and for itself passes over into [p. 283] universality, just as the form of intuition, of immediate knowing and determinate being, passes over into the self-mediating knowing, into a determinate being that is itself knowing, into the revealing. b. §. 465. Absolute spirit in this stage of the sublated immediacy of its shape and of its knowing, thus at the stage of reflection, is on the one hand universal spirit of nature and of spirit, being in and for itself, but on the other hand it is for representation; the subjectivity of knowing, because it is reflection, gives to the moments of spirit's life, whose totality spirit essentially is, independence, and makes them, against one another, into presuppositions and successive appearances, and into a connection of occurrence according to finite determinations of reflection. §. 466. In its separating, reflection separates the form from the content, and in the former the distinct moments of the Concept off, as particular spheres or elements, in each of which the absolute content presents itself.

e: concretion dying away into the absolute pain of negativity, and, as identical with itself in it, thus having become for itself out of it as absolute return and universal unity of universal and singular essentiality, — the Idea of spirit as eternal but living and actual. §. 470. β) This totality is, because it is itself still in the sphere of reflection, the one that is in itself, or presupposition, and over against it stand the separation and finite immediacy of singular subjectivity. For this, that first presupposition and its movement is at first an other and something intuited, but the intuition of its truth that is in itself, whereby this finite subject, on account of its immediate nature, determines itself for itself as the null and evil. It is therefore, after the example of its truth, the movement to divest itself of its immediate natural determinacy and of its own will, and to unite itself with that in the pain of negativity, in the universal abstraction, and so to cognize itself as identical with the essence, which γ) through this mediation effects itself as indwelling in self-consciousness and is the actual universal spirit. §. 471. The revelation of the absolute, which presents its life in a cycle of concrete shapes of representation, takes the same together, out of their diverging independence and temporal and external succession, in this their last result as the true and the actual, into the universal, simple and eternal spirit; in this form of truth, truth is the object of philosophy.

e: c. §. 472. It is the unity of art and religion insofar as the simple intuition and substantial production of the former, through the diverging and the mediation of the latter, has been raised to self-conscious thinking. In this element the self-conscious Idea purifies itself just as much of its first immediacy as also of the semblance of occurrence, of contingency and of being outside and after one another, which its content has in the second. This knowing is thus the Concept of art and religion, in which what is different in that content is cognized as necessary, and this necessary and the immediate as free. §. 473. This cognition of the necessity of the content of absolute representation, as well as of the necessity of the two forms, of immediate intuition and its poetry on the one hand, and on the other of presupposing representation, of objective and external revelation, and of the subjective movement toward and inner identifying of faith with it, the recognition of the content and of the form, and the liberation from these forms, finds itself already accomplished, in that philosophy at the close grasps its own Concept, i.e. only looks back on its knowing. §. 474.

Diese Erscheinung macht zuerst der Schluß aus , welcher das Logische zum Grunde als ersten Ausgangspunkte, und die Natur zur Mitte hat, die den Geist mit demselben zusammenschließt Das Logische. wird zur Natur und die Natur zum Geiste, Die. Natur die zwischen dem Geiste und seinem Wesen steht;,, trennt sie zwar nicht zu Extremen endlicher Abstraction, denn der Schluß ist in der Idee, und die Natur wesentlich nur als Durchgangspunkt und negatives Moment, die bestimmt; aber die Vermittlung des Begriffs hat äusserliche Erscheinung der Form des Uebergehens und Wissenschaft die eines Senns. §. 476. - Diese Erscheinung ist im zweyten Schlusse aufgehoben, in welchem der Geist das Vermittelnde ist; ein Schluß, der bereits der Standpunkt des Geistes selbst ist, welcher die Natur voraussekt und sie mit dem Logischen zusammenschließt. Es ist der Schluß der Reflexion in der Idee; die Wissenschaft erscheint als ein subjectives Erkennen. §. 477.
e: This its Concept is the Idea thinking itself, the knowing truth (§ 183) or the logical with [p. 287] the meaning that it is the universality verified in the concrete content. Science has in this way returned into its beginning, and the logical is its result; the presupposition of its Concept or the immediacy of its beginning, and the side of appearance which it had in it, is sublated. §. 475. This appearance is constituted first by the syllogism which has the logical as ground, as first point of departure, and nature as middle term, which joins spirit together with it. The logical becomes nature, and nature spirit. Nature, which stands between spirit and its essence, does indeed not separate them into extremes of finite abstraction; for the syllogism is in the Idea, and nature is determined essentially only as point of passage and negative moment; but the mediation of the Concept has the external appearance of the form of passing over, and science that of a being. §. 476. This appearance is sublated in the second syllogism, in which spirit is the mediating; — a syllogism that is already the standpoint of spirit itself, which presupposes nature and joins it together with the logical. It is the syllogism of reflection in the Idea; science appears as a subjective cognition. §. 477.

o: Diese Erscheinungen sind in der Idee der Philosophie aufgehoben, welche die sich wissende Vernunft, das, absolut = Algemeine zu ihrer Mitte hat, die sich in Geist und Natur entzweyt 1, jenen [p. 288] me macht. Als solches ist die Natur unmittelbar nur ein Gesektes, wie der Geist eben dieß so ihm an selbst nicht die Voraussekung sondern die, sich zuin rückgekehrte Totalität zu seyn. Auf diese Weise hat die Mitte, der wissende Begriff, schlechthin solche, welche als Begriffsmomente sind, zu seiner Realität und ist als das allgemeine in seiner Bestimmtheit unmittelbar bey sich bleibende Wissen. e: These appearances are sublated in the Idea of philosophy, which has as its middle term the self-knowing reason, the absolutely universal, which divides itself into spirit and nature, and makes the former [p. 288] its presupposition and the latter the universal extreme. As such, nature is immediately only something posited, just as spirit, in its own self, is precisely this: to be not the presupposition but the totality returned into itself. In this way the middle, the knowing Concept, has as its reality simply those which are as moments of the Concept, and is the knowing that, as the universal, remains immediately with itself in its determinacy.
